pr.title: Add request client with retries and failure tests
pr.author: Alex Morgan
pr.description: Introduces a typed request boundary, applies retry behavior, and documents failure semantics in tests.

summary.overview: The PR moves request policy into one typed client, connects it to the existing hook, and proves how terminal failures reach callers.
summary.reviewStrategy: Read the public contract first, then the runtime lifecycle, and finish with the tests that define its failure boundary.
summary.risk: Retry and cancellation behavior can subtly change request timing or duplicate non-idempotent work.

parts.title: Establish the request contract
parts.summary: Creates the stable boundary consumed by the hook and exercised by tests.
parts.whatChanged: The client now accepts typed options, applies explicit timeout and retry defaults, and normalizes terminal failures into RequestError.
parts.whyThisApproach: A transport-neutral contract keeps callers from depending directly on fetch details and gives tests one observable failure shape.
reviewFocus: Do the new defaults preserve the behavior existing callers expect?
Can every terminal transport failure be represented by RequestError?
Is the retry option safe for every supported HTTP method?

parts.title: Wire the request lifecycle
parts.summary: Moves the hook onto the shared client while preserving its UI-facing state machine.
parts.whatChanged: useRequest delegates transport work to the new client and only publishes data from the latest invocation.
parts.whyThisApproach: Keeping sequencing in the hook prevents an older retrying request from overwriting the result of a newer one.
reviewFocus: Does the request ID guard cover both successful and failed stale requests?
Is cancellation still observable by consumers?
Can retry delay keep the hook in a loading state indefinitely?

annotations.title: Keep the latest request in control
annotations.body: The request ID comparison appears intended to prevent an older invocation from publishing success over a newer request. Verify whether a new request can start during the awaited response decoding.

parts.title: Prove the failure path
parts.summary: Makes timeout exhaustion and stale-response behavior explicit at the test boundary.
parts.whatChanged: The test suite adds deterministic cases for retry exhaustion and for a superseded request resolving late.
parts.whyThisApproach: The tests assert externally visible outcomes instead of internal retry-loop steps, leaving room to change the transport implementation.
reviewFocus: Do the fake timers model production scheduling accurately?
Would the tests catch an extra network attempt?
Is the original failure retained as the error cause?
